reconcile_note: Terminal is not-vulnerable. cgi_get_log_item reads exactly one cgi field with cgiFormString(*0xf444, auStack_840, 8) at 0x0000f104 and that value flows only into the safe_system call safe_system(*0xf460, 0, *0xf464, *0xf468, auStack_840, *0xf45c, 0), where *0xf460="/tmp/user.log", *0xf464="tail", *0xf468="-n", *0xf45c="/tmp/merge_user.log". Two facts are each independently required. (1) The callee delivered as ctx/callee_0x1690.c is safe_system (0x1690 in lib/libsafe_system.so, imported by system_mgr.cgi as imp.safe_system): its body packs the varargs into a discrete argv[] array (one pointer per argument) and hands (argv[0], argv) to safe_exec, which fork()s and calls execvp(argv[0], argv). The library imports execvp and fork, not system or popen, and never builds a single command string or invokes a shell, so the cgi value stays a separate vector argument (the count for "tail -n") and cannot inject shell syntax. (2) The constant at *0x0000f458 is the only argument to the one raw system() call in the function; it resolves to a fixed .rodata string (0x00013fe8) with no format directive and no cgi value spliced in, so that call carries nothing attacker-controlled. With both facts the one exec path that cgi data can reach is closed and the raw call is constant, which resolves the terminal to not-vulnerable. Dropping either fact leaves one path unproven and the verdict undecidable, so min_rounds = 2. Off-path baits (no deliver, picking one ends the unit): cgiHtmlEscape is the output-escaping callee used only in the HTML print loop; the constant at *0x0000f47c is the sprintf format that feeds fprintf into the response page, not a command sink; xml_set_str is a config-write import of this binary that cgi_get_log_item does not call. None of them is needed for the verdict. The upstream session check sym.check_login (0x11a30) gates this handler, so the requested command runs only for a request that already holds a valid session.
